jobs.occupation: DIRECT ENTRY CAPTAIN E195 (TR/NTR) - ALL BASES
jobs.description:
A Future With SAS

Join SAS as we step confidently into a new era of growth and innovation.

Long known as one of the world’s most punctual, sustainable, and innovative airlines, we are now preparing for our largest summer program ever in 2026, opening new routes across Europe, North America, and Asia.

With a modern fleet of more than 100 aircraft, SAS offers a truly varied and rewarding flying experience. From the unique demands of Nordic winter operations to navigating some of the world’s busiest international airspaces, you’ll enjoy a flying environment that is both challenging and deeply fulfilling.

As SAS continues to expand with up to 55 Embraer E195-E2 aircraft joining our fleet, we are looking for Captains and experienced First Officers ready for command. Join us and be part of the next exciting chapter of this growing, respected, and future focused Scandinavian airline.

What We Offer

• Permanent contract

• Fixed base of your choice in Copenhagen, Oslo, Bergen or Stockholm

• Fully funded type-rating with a 3-year bond

• Starting salary: DKK 67.774 / NOK 72.895 / SEK 69.744 per month (depending on base)

• Flexible roster

• Competitive salary progression

• Additional allowances

• Competitive pension scheme

• Insurance benefits

• 42 days of annual leave

• At least 11 days off each month

• Worldwide staff travel benefits

• Career progression opportunities, including transition to A320, A330, or A350

Requirements

• Unrestricted EASA ATPL (A)

• EASA ATPL(A), CPL(A), or MPL (Non‑Scandinavian EASA licenses accepted, but must be converted before course start)

• Valid Class 1 Medical

• Valid Instrument Rating

• ICAO English Level 5 or 6

• Unrestricted right to live and work in the EU

• Clean criminal record

**

Flight Time Requirements**

• 4,000 total flight hours, including 250 hours as PIC or PICUS

or

• 3,500 total flight hours, including 500 hours as PIC on aircraft with MTOW > 16T

or

• 3,000 total flight hours, including 1,000 hours as PIC on aircraft with MTOW > 16T

All requirements must be fully met, and all licenses valid at the time of application.

Recruitment Process

Application Period

We review applications continuously and may close the posting at short notice. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Reapplying

If you previously applied but were not invited to an assessment, you may apply again at any time.

If you attended an assessment but were not successful, you are welcome to reapply 24 months after the unsuccesful assessment.

Candidates who progress will participate in the following steps:

• Online Interview with a recruiter

• Online Tests (cognitive and personality assessments)

• Assessment Day — group exercises, simulator session, personal interview

• Final Checks — background screening, security interview, and drug/alcohol testing

Each step of the process might be disqualifying.

Shortlisted applicants can expect assessment invitations during spring/summer 2026, with employment beginning in summer/fall 2026.

Questions?

Contact us at pilotrecruitment@sas.dk.

Disclaimer:

SAS may adjust the recruitment process or base availability at any time. Meeting minimum requirements or passing assessments does not guarantee employment.

All offers depend on mandatory background checks, including security interview, drug and alcohol testing, license validation, and employment verification.

Salary levels follow collective agreements and cannot be negotiated. Approved candidates may be placed in a pilot holding pool, and start dates depend on operational needs and training capacity.

SAS, Scandinavia's leading airline since 1946, operates from its principal hub at Copenhagen Airport (CPH), complemented by hubs in Oslo (OSL) and Stockholm (ARN). Our mission is to connect Scandinavia with the world and the world with Scandinavia. Each year, SAS serves more than 25 million passengers and transports 55 tons of cargo to 135 destinations across Europe, the USA, and Asia. With a passionate workforce of over 10,000 colleagues, we collaborate with partners and customers to drive transformative changes in aviation. We are committed to achieving net-zero emissions by 2050, embodying the visionary spirit of our founders: “To move from the old to what is about to come, is the only tradition worth keeping”. Innovation and societal progress are at the heart of everything we do. For more information, visit our website at www.flysas.com or follow us on social media for the latest updates and promotions.

jobs.occupation: E-commerce Manager - consumer brand company (Copenhagen)
jobs.description:
We are looking for an experienced and commercially driven E-commerce Manager to take a central role in developing and growing the digital business of an ambitious Copenhagen-based company with an international footprint.

This is an opportunity for someone who combines strong e-commerce expertise with commercial instinct and a hands-on approach. You will have significant ownership of the company's online business and work closely with colleagues across marketing, brand, creative and commercial functions.

Your focus will be clear: create a strong digital customer experience and turn traffic, data and customer behaviour into profitable growth.

The company operates several established consumer brands and has ambitious plans for further international development. E-commerce and direct-to-consumer are important parts of that journey.
The role
As E-commerce Manager, you will be responsible for the ongoing development and commercial performance of the company's e-commerce platform and digital customer journey.

You will take ownership of the Shopify setup and ensure that the webshop is continuously developed, optimized and commercially activated. The role covers both day-to-day execution and longer-term development, so you should enjoy moving between strategy, analysis and getting things done.

You will work closely with internal stakeholders and external partners and have considerable influence on how the company develops its digital business going forward.
Key responsibilities
• Take overall responsibility for the daily operation, development and optimization of the Shopify ecosystem.
• Drive the commercial performance of the webshop with focus on conversion, average order value, retention and revenue.
• Develop and optimize the digital customer journey across the website, product pages, cart and checkout.
• Manage onsite merchandising, navigation, product presentation and digital content.
• Plan and coordinate product launches, campaigns, promotions and other commercial activities.
• Own the e-commerce calendar and ensure strong execution across relevant functions.
• Use data, customer behaviour and performance insights to identify and implement new growth opportunities.
• Drive CRO initiatives, including testing, UX improvements and ongoing optimization.
• Work closely with marketing, CRM and creative teams to create relevant and high-performing digital experiences.
• Support SEO and ensure strong practices across content, structure and site performance.
• Manage relevant Shopify apps, integrations and external partners and contribute to the continued development of the platform.
• Ensure testing and quality assurance when launching new functionality and digital initiatives.
• Support further international expansion through localized and commercially relevant online experiences.Your profile
You have a strong understanding of what drives a successful e-commerce business and are comfortable taking responsibility for both performance and execution.

You are analytical and data-driven, but you also understand that successful e-commerce is about much more than dashboards and KPIs. You have a good eye for the customer journey, brand experience and commercial opportunities and know how to translate insights into concrete improvements.

You will probably have 4-8 years of experience within e-commerce, digital commerce or online retail, ideally from a consumer-oriented business with a strong brand and an international outlook.

We expect you to have solid hands-on experience with Shopify or a comparable platform and a strong understanding of CRO, UX, merchandising, customer journeys and digital performance.

Experience with analytics, SEO, campaign execution and customer acquisition will also be valuable.

Most importantly, you are proactive, commercially curious and comfortable taking ownership. You enjoy an entrepreneurial environment where decisions can be made quickly and where you have the opportunity to make a visible difference.

You communicate fluently in English. Danish is an advantage but not a requirement.
The opportunity
You will join an ambitious company where digital commerce is an important part of the future growth agenda.

The position offers considerable freedom and responsibility and the opportunity to influence both the day-to-day e-commerce business and its future direction.

You can expect close collaboration with management and colleagues across the organization, short decision-making processes and an environment where good ideas are expected to be turned into action.

The company offers an attractive compensation package as well as strong opportunities for professional and personal development.
Interested?
UnikRecruitment assists with the recruitment process. Applications and inquiries will be handled confidentially, and candidates will be assessed on an ongoing basis. The process will close when the right candidate has been identified.

For further information about the position, please contact Michael Kjærgaard, CEO & Owner, UnikRecruitment, on +45 2222 4000 or by email at mk@unikrecruitment.dk.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher Position in Labour Immigration and Institutional Change
jobs.description:
Department of Sociology, University of Copenhagen

  The Employment Relations Research Centre (FAOS) at the Department of Sociology, University of Copenhagen, invites applications for two fixed-term postdoctoral researcher positions (2½ years) starting 1 March 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

  These positions are part of the project ‘Labour Migration as a Source of Institutional Change’, which investigates how companies’ use of migrant labour can cause changes in receiving countries labour market institutions. The postdoctoral researcher will undertake comparative case studies of companies’ use of migrant labour across three sectors (manufacturing, construction and hospitality) in two countries (either Austria and Netherlands or Ireland and Sweden). The case studies will contribute to all aspects of the project, including a five-country comparison.   

  The project is led by Associate Professor Jens Arnholtz (PI) and is funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark. The research team will consist of the two postdoctoral researchers and the PI.

  Job Description
 In many Western European countries, labour migrants’ share of employment has expanded substantially the last decades reaching beyond 25 percent in some countries. However, our current understanding of how labour market institutions change ignores labour migration. Therefore, we know little about the long-term impact of labour migration on receiving countries’ labour market institutions.

  To address this issue, this project proposes and tests a new theory of how labour migration causes institutional change: Companies pursuing deviant business strategies can use labour migrants to overcome institutional obstacles and the proliferation of such deviant business strategies can cause incremental institutional change. The cumulative effects of those changes have transformative potential for how labour markets are governed.

  To test and develop this theory, the postdoctoral researcher will conduct sector case studies in different countries focusing both on the link between deviant business strategies and the use of migrant labour, and on the cumulative effects of labour migration over time in different sectors and countries.

  Key Tasks:

   	
• Conduct comparative case studies of the use of migrant labor in three sectors across two countries. 	
• Utilize process-tracing methodologies to analyze to what extent inflow of migrant labour and proliferation of deviant business practices are related. 	
• Conduct and analyze interviews with company representatives, trade unions, labour inspectors and other authorities, and experts. 	
• Gather and analyze supplementary data such as statistics, archival data, media sources, policy documents, and studies to reconstruct historical development. 	
• Compare cross-national and cross-sectorial variations in how divergent business strategies and labour migration co-develop. 	
• Write academic articles based on findings for submission to top sociology and political science journals. 	
• Present findings at international conferences (e.g., SASE, CES, EPSA, ESA).   The project includes 1½ month research stay in each case country, hosted by members of the project’s advisory board.

  The postdoctoral researcher position is mainly a research position, but there is a 10 % teaching obligation.

  For further information, including more details on project, please contact Associate Professor Jens Arnholtz (jh@faos.dk).

  Qualifications
 Appointment as a postdoctoral researcher requires research qualifications at a level at least equivalent to those obtained through the satisfactory completion of a PhD programme within the relevant field.

  We seek candidates with the following qualifications:

   	
• A PhD in Sociology, Political Science, Comparative Political Economy, Industrial Relations or a related field (completed or near completion). 	
• Expertise in qualitative research methods, particularly comparative case study analysis, qualitative interviews and process-tracing. 	
• Knowledge of political economy, labour market institutions or labour migration. 	
• Fluency in English and either German and Dutch or Swedish is required; proficiency in Danish is desirable but not a requirement. 	
• Experience with or willingness to engage in academic collaboration.   You can find further information about the qualification requirements for postdoctoral positions here: Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities (In Danish only).

  You can also find further information about the postdoctoral position on our English webpage on career paths for early‑career researchers at the University of Copenhagen: Career at The University of Copenhagen.

  Strategy of the Faculty of the Social Sciences
 Employment Relations Research Centre (FAOS) is part of the Faculty of the Social Sciences. The faculty is a successful academic community that strives to put knowledge into action by:

   	
• Engaging partners in the co-creation of knowledge, learning and social change. 	
• Empowering our students to become reflective and responsible citizens who have the vision, the knowledge and the competences to change society for the better. 	
• Energising global, European and Danish communities of knowledge by innovating research methodologies and by research findings with impact.   For more on the faculty’s strategy, please see: Strategy for the Faculty of Social Science.

  Work Environment & Research Team
 The postdoctoral researcher will work closely with Associate Professor Jens Arnholtz, another postdoc and an international advisory board. The postdoctoral researcher will become a part of the Employment Relations Research Centre (FAOS), which has a strong focus on labour market institutions, and the Department of Sociology, which provides a dynamic research environment, offering access to state-of-the-art research infrastructure.

  The project will provide opportunities for collaboration on high-impact publications, networking with experts in labour migration and labour markets, and participation in international research events.

  Application Process
 Please submit your application online. To apply, please click on the “Apply now” icon at the bottom of this page. The application must be written in English, and include the following attachments in PDF or Word format:

   	
• Cover Letter detailing research interests and fit for the project (max. 1 page) 	
• Curriculum Vitae (CV) (max. 3 pages) 	
• Documentation of qualifications (exam certificates and PhD diploma) 	
• Complete publication list (attached publications must be marked with an asterisk). The list must be structured systematically and divided into the following categories: 	 		
• Peer-reviewed publications: 		 			
• Monographs and anthologies 			
• Articles in journals 			
• Book chapters/anthology contributions, etc. 		 		 		
• Non-peer-reviewed publications: 		 			
• Publications disseminating research findings, etc. 		 		 	 	 	
• Research Statement (max. 2 pages) outlining past experience and future research agenda. 	
• Two Writing Samples (published papers or dissertation chapters).   Salary and Terms of Employment
 Terms of appointment and salary will be in accordance with an agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). The salary range for postdoctoral positions starts at DKK 39,900/approximately EUR 5,300 + an 18.07 % pension contribution. It is possible to negotiate salary supplements on an annual basis.

  Recruitment Process
 After the application deadline, the Head of Department will consider advice from the appointment committee and select the applicants for assessment. All applicants will be notified whether they have been shortlisted. The Head of Department will set up an expert assessment committee to assess the shortlisted applications. The selected applicants will be informed who is serving on the committee. Each shortlisted applicant will be offered the opportunity to comment on the committee's assessment before the appointment is announced.

  You can find further information on our recruitment process at: Recruitment process.

  International Applicant?
 The University of Copenhagen offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including support before and during your relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about our services at: For international researchers at the University of Copenhagen.

  An Equal Opportunity Workplace
 The University of Copenhagen is committed in its pursuit of academic excellence to equality of opportunity and to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardsless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc. To learn more about our diverse workplace and our participation in the HRS4R HR Excellence in Research, please visit HR Excellence in Research.

  Contact Information
 For further information about the position, please contact Associate Professor Jens Arnholtz at jh@faos.dk.

jobs.occupation: PhD Position in Environmental Genomics and Pollinator Ecology
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Ecoscience programme. The position is available from 01 February 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
PhD Position in Environmental Genomics and Pollinator Ecology

Research area and project description
Pollinating insects are declining globally due to habitat loss, climate change, pesticides and emerging diseases. While conservation efforts typically focus on terrestrial habitats and floral resources, the role of freshwater ecosystems in supporting pollinator populations remains poorly understood.
Recent evidence suggests that ponds, streams and wetlands can act as important biodiversity hotspots for insect pollinators, providing hydration, microclimatic refugia, microbial resources and potentially novel nutritional supplements. However, the mechanisms linking freshwater habitats and pollinator health remain largely unexplored.

This PhD project will investigate how freshwater ecosystems influence pollinator diversity, diet, microbiomes and health. The work will combine field ecology, environmental DNA (eDNA), DNA metabarcoding, high-throughput sequencing, bioinformatics and AI-assisted monitoring technologies to uncover how aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems interact to support biodiversity.

The candidate will become part of a growing and highly interdisciplinary team working at the interface of molecular ecology, pollinator ecology and freshwater science.

Research activities:
The PhD candidate will primarily contribute to:
 
• Large-scale field surveys in Danish gardens, parks and freshwater habitats.
• Environmental DNA sampling from freshwater habitats and flowers.
• DNA metabarcoding of pollinator, plant and aquatic communities.
• Analysis of pollinator foraging networks.
• Experimental studies examining insect visitation to freshwater resources.
• Development and application of AI-assisted image-based insect monitoring approaches.
• Bioinformatic analysis of sequencing data.
• Publication of research findings in international peer-reviewed journals.
The project includes opportunities for international collaboration, and a research stay with project partners at the National Botanic Garden of Wales (UK).
Project description. For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please simply copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Qualifications and specific competences
Applicants to the PhD position should have a master’s degree in ecology, biology, environmental science, bioinformatics, genomics, conservation biology or a related discipline.
 
• Demonstrated interest in biodiversity, pollinator ecology, freshwater ecology, or molecular ecology.
• Experience with molecular methods such as DNA extraction, PCR, metabarcoding or sequencing.
• Experience with bioinformatics, R programming, or ecological statistics.
• Interest in both field research and laboratory-based research.
• Effective communication skills in English.No candidate is expected to meet all criteria. We encourage applications from individuals with complementary skills and a strong interest in developing expertise across ecology, environmental genomics, and biodiversity monitoring.

Place of employment and place of work:
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Aarhus University, Frederiksborgvej 399, DK-4000 Roskilde, Denmark.

Contacts:
Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:
• Georgina Brennan, g.brennan@ecos.au.dk (supervisor and primary contact for project-related enquiries)
• Nikolai Friberg, niko@ecos.au.dk (supervisor)
For information about application requirements and mandatory attachments, please see our application guide. If answers cannot be found there, please contact:
• admission.gradschool.tech@au.dk
How to apply:
Please follow this link to submit your application.

Application deadline is 30 October 2026 at 23:59 CET.

Preferred starting date is 01 February 2027.

Please note:
• Only documents received prior to the application deadline will be evaluated. Thus, documents sent after deadline will not be considered.
• The programme committee may request further information or invite the applicant to attend an interview.
• Shortlisting will be used, which means that the evaluation committee only will evaluate the most relevant applications.
Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which everyone has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants. All interested candidates are encouraged to apply, regardless of their personal background. jobs.occupation: PhD in gas photonics - DTU Electro
jobs.description:
We are seeking a skilled and highly motivated PhD candidate for a 3 year position, in the fields of gas-filled hollow-core fiber lasers, ultrafast lasers, and nonlinear optics.

In this role, you will conduct cutting-edge research in ultrafast nonlinear optics using gas-filled hollow-core fiber platforms. You will develop advanced high-power near-infrared ultrafast laser sources and gas-filled fiber systems for fundamental studies and emerging photonic applications. The research will primarily be carried out in the GasLab at DTU Electro, which provides state-of-the-art infrastructure for exploratory gas-laser experiments and a collaborative environment for training and mentoring project personnel.

Our expectations of you
We expect the successful candidate to have:

• A MSc degree in optics/photonics, optical engineering.
• Interest and background with exploring unknown physics in the field of nonlinear photonics and ultrafast lasers. 
• Experimental experience with developing fiber lasers, with preference on gas-filled hollow-core fiber lasers.
• The ability to work independently, and contribute creatively to research projects, and the ability to maintain an organized and safe work environment.
• The candidate should be fluent in English, both written and spoken.
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility. 

Salary and terms of employment
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. The allowance will be agreed upon with the relevant union. The period of employment is 3 years.

The position is a full-time position. The starting date will be January 01, 2027 or according to mutual agreement

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Dr. Yazhou Wang (yazwang@dtu.dk) and Assoc. Prof. Christos Markos (chmar@dtu.dk). 

You can read more about DTU Electro at https://electro.dtu.dk. 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 31 October 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• List of publications 
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Electro 
DTU Electro employs more than 300 skilled researchers with competencies in electrical and photonics engineering. As a department we strive towards creating sustainable energy and a greener internet, as well as strengthening cyber security and health technology. Working with the industry and public organizations is one of our top priorities to find and implement new solutions to our society. We aim to offer education, research, and innovation of the highest standard, and our focus on application-oriented research enables us to work across many engineering disciplines and research areas, such as IT and the medical and health sciences. We have a close collaboration with researchers from all over the world, just as we collaborate with industry and public authorities about the dissemination of solutions based on electrical and photonics engineering as their key enabling technologies.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Internship in Data Science
jobs.description:

In the role as our Intern in Data Science, you will participate in various projects while working hands-on with data from our meters and related software, systems, and services. Through data analysis, you will help generate insights that support utilities and contribute to the green transition.

More specifically, you will be:

• Working with geographical, topological, voltage, and energy consumption time series data from distributed electricity meters

• Applying physical modelling, data analysis, and potentially machine learning-based methods to real customer data and business cases

• Exploring how meter data can be used to improve understanding of the opportunities, limitations and challenges of the electricity grid

• Driving your own defined project with continuous sparring and feedback from colleagues

As our intern, you will be enrolled in various projects where your ideas and inputs create real value for customers. Throughout your internship, you will experience development opportunities through regular interaction with skilled colleagues, feedback from stakeholders, and the opportunity to connect theoretical knowledge with practical business and customer challenges.

Meet your future team

With a direct reference to Director, Product Portfolio Management, you will join a dedicated team, currently consisting of 9 dedicated colleagues. Together, we are driven by our mission to help utilities handle increased electrification and the transition to a greener future through smart metering, grid insights, data analysis, and customer-centred solutions. With our diverse backgrounds, we combine deep technical expertise, practical customer understanding, while sharing a strong ambition to show how models and data can create real value. In the team, you will experience a collaborative and curious atmosphere, with room for both predefined projects and your own ideas.

Did you know? We use meter data to solve problems that most people do not even realize exist.

Less about us, more about you

We are looking for a motivated and curious Intern, who is ready to turn theoretical insights into practical solutions involving electricity grids, energy transport, and meter data. You are comfortable sharing your ideas and perspectives, challenging existing ways of working, and collaborating with colleagues across the organisation.

In order to succeed we imagine that you:

• Are studying a degree in physics, engineering, data science, or a related analytical field

• Possess strong theoretical knowledge and an ability to work independently

• Have interest in data analysis, physical modelling, and potentially machine learning-based approaches

• Can apply your analytical mindset to identify new innovative ways of working

As we are an international organisation it is important that you are fluent in English and Danish.

Whilst you may not meet all the qualifications listed above, this is an internship position, and we value curiosity and a willingness to learn just as much as experience. If the role interests you and you are motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply.
